land.text: 'The Tepanec lands were carved up among the three cities'

successors.note: 'In 1428, Maxtla was overthrown by the nascent Aztec Triple Alliance'; infobox 'Incorporated into Aztec Empire: 1428'. Tlacopan, the dissident Tepanec city, became the junior partner.

capitals.name: Azcapotzalco
capitals.note: 'the main altepetl' of the Tepanec territory (Tepanec page); no capital is named. Azcapotzalco is not in the gazetteer; the coordinates are the town's (Mexico City borough), not from a page.

rulers.name: Acolnahuacatl
rulers.note: Chimalpahin's dates: 'Acolnahuacatl ruled from 1302 to 1366 and Tezozomoc 1367 to 1426'; some historians place Acolnahuacatl's death and Tezozomoc's rise in 1371. Rulers before 1302 are not on the pages.

rulers.name: Tezozomoc
rulers.note: 'During his reign (ca. 1371-1426), Azcapotzalco reached its greatest splendor.'

rulers.name: Maxtla
rulers.note: 'The death of Tezozomoc in 1426 brought his sons Tayatzin and Maxtla to the throne'; Maxtla 'most likely poisoned Tayatzin'; he was overthrown in 1428.

correction.text: The altepetl of Azcapotzalco on the western shore of Lake Texcoco: 'Azcapotzalco was founded by Chichimecs in the year 995 AD'; 'the Tepanec took over Azcapotzalco from its inhabitants under Acolnahuacatl'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks Azcapotzalco). The pages give no area; a 12 km disc stands for the altepetl. The Tepanec arrival is 'in the late 12th or early 13th centuries' (footnote dates 1152, 1210, 1226), against the founding of 995 in Chimalpahin's account; the founding year is the Azcapotzalco page's and is doubtful. Fix fx-40: `to` 1376, because the Colhuacan keyframe now starts in 1377.

union.text: Colhuacan (Culhuacan), a chinampa town of the southern valley now inside Mexico City; the gazetteer has no place 'Colhuacan' and the pages give no coordinates, so the Mexico City admin-1 (4 cells) stands in

correction.text: Azcapotzalco with Colhuacan, 'together conquered ... in 1385' (Azcapotzalco page) or subdued 'in 1377 ... in large part with Aztec troops' (Colhuacan page); the Mexico City admin-1 stands in for the unresolvable place 'Colhuacan'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Tezozomoc's expansion starts: 'together conquered the city of Colhuacan in 1385'. The other Tepanec conquests (Chalco, Xochimilco, Coyoacan, Morelos) are not on the pages; the shape grows to the whole Valley in 1414. Fix fx-40 (2 Nov 2026), R049: `from` moved from 1385 to 1377 and the region 'Colhuacan' (8 km, unknown to the gazetteer, so the keyframe never applied) replaced by the Mexico City admin-1, as in the p1300-p1399 patch (keyframe_overrides/5, same spec). Colhuacan page: 'in 1377 Azcapotzalco subdued Culhuacan in large part with Aztec troops'; Azcapotzalco page: 'together conquered the city of Colhuacan in 1385'. The shape_id keeps its 1385 label.

correction.text: 'Between 1414-1418, Azcapotzalco controlled the entire Valley of Mexico'; the Tepanec empire controlled 'nearly all of the Valley of Mexico and parts of the Toluca and Morelos valleys'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1414-1428 (the page's span is 1414-1418; the Tepanec page's extent is undated and the empire stands to its overthrow in 1428, so 1419-1428 is my reading). The infobox gives no area. Tenochtitlan was a tributary; Texcoco is drawn as a contest from 1418; the Toluca and Morelos parts are left out.

ledger.note: 995: Chichimecs found Azcapotzalco. 'Azcapotzalco was founded by Chichimecs in the year 995 AD' (Chimalpahin's account; infobox 'Established: 995'). The Tepanec page dates the Tepanec arrival to the late 12th or early 13th century, so 995 is doubtful.

1325: the Mexica of Tenochtitlan are Tepanec tributaries. 'In 1318 for the first time they attacked the Aztecs, which resulted in an increased tribute' (Azcapotzalco page); 'Under Itzcoatl, the Mexica of Tenochtitlan broke free from Tepanec domination' (Itzcoatl page). No start year is given; 1325 is the founding of Tenochtitlan (page silent, confidence 1).

region.text: Colhuacan (Culhuacan), a chinampa town of the southern valley now inside Mexico City; the gazetteer has no place 'Colhuacan' and the pages give no coordinates, so the Mexico City admin-1 (4 cells) stands in

ledger.note: 1377: Colhuacan falls to Azcapotzalco. Colhuacan (altepetl) page, opened 2 Nov 2026: 'Nevertheless, in 1377 Azcapotzalco subdued Culhuacan in large part with Aztec troops', many Culhua seeking refuge in Acolhuacan, Azcapotzalco and Cuauhtitlan. The Azcapotzalco (altepetl) page, also opened 2 Nov 2026, says 'Tezozomoc forced the Aztecs to fight with him and together conquered the city of Colhuacan in 1385'; the pages disagree by eight years and the dossier now follows the page about the conquered city (1377), which also names the Mexica as the partner. Fix fx-40, window request R049: the place 'Colhuacan' (8 km) is not in the gazetteer, so the event used to be skipped; neither page gives coordinates or a borough, and the Mexico City admin-1 (the stand-in the p1300-p1399 patch uses, its events/3) is the nearest named unit.

1414: Azcapotzalco rules the whole Valley of Mexico. 'Between 1414-1418, Azcapotzalco controlled the entire Valley of Mexico.' The conquests of Chalco, Xochimilco and Coyoacan are not dated on the pages.

1418: Tezozomoc dethrones Ixtlilxochitl I of Texcoco. 'In 1418, Ixtlilxochitl I, the tlatoani (ruler) of Tetzcoco, was dethroned by Tezozomoc of Azcapotzalco.' The contest runs to 1428. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region now excludes the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan), which the 30 km Texcoco disc reached]

1427: the Mexica, Texcoco, Tlacopan and Huexotzinco go to war against Azcapotzalco. 'In 1427, Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan, and Huexotzinco went to war against Azcapotzalco, emerging victorious in 1428.' Maxtla had succeeded Tezozomoc in 1426.
1428: the Mexica throw off the Tepanec yoke. 'Under Itzcoatl, the Mexica of Tenochtitlan broke free from Tepanec domination.'
1428: Texcoco is freed. 'emerging victorious in 1428'. [Reviewer am-03, 2026-10-18: region now excludes the Mexico City cell (Tenochtitlan), which the 30 km Texcoco disc reached]
1428: the war ends with the sack of Azcapotzalco. 'Together they attacked and sacked Azcapotzalco in 1428.'

region.text: the Tepanec lands, 'carved up among the three cities'

ledger.note: 1428: Azcapotzalco loses its empire. 'The Tepanec lands were carved up among the three cities' of the Triple Alliance; 'In 1428, Maxtla was overthrown by the nascent Aztec Triple Alliance'.
1428: the Tepanec empire ends. Infobox 'Incorporated into Aztec Empire: 1428'; 'Tlacopan became the predominant Tepanec city' under the Aztec empire (Tepanec page).

wars.name: Tepanec War
wars.outcome: Azcapotzalco sacked in 1428 and its empire carved up among Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan.
wars.note: Tezozomoc died in 1426; Maxtla usurped the throne and Chimalpopoca of Tenochtitlan died shortly after; Nezahualcoyotl of Texcoco 'fled into exile' and recruited help from Huexotzinco.

wars.name: Tepanec conquest of Colhuacan

zones.text: Colhuacan (Culhuacan); the Mexico City admin-1 stands in for the place the gazetteer lacks

wars.outcome: Colhuacan conquered: 'in 1377 Azcapotzalco subdued Culhuacan in large part with Aztec troops' (Colhuacan page); the Azcapotzalco page has 'together conquered the city of Colhuacan in 1385'.

certainty.note: A tributary empire of altepetl; no border is known. The Valley of Mexico shape for 1414-1428 is the page's 'entire Valley' and is soft.

sources.title: Azcapotzalco (altepetl)
sources.note: Founding 995, rulers' dates, 1385 Colhuacan, 1414-1418 the entire Valley, 1428 sack and incorporation.

sources.title: Tepanec
sources.note: Arrival in the 12th-13th century, Tezozomoc's height, 1426 death, Maxtla overthrown in 1428, Tlacopan.

sources.title: Colhuacan (altepetl)
sources.note: Fix fx-40: 'in 1377 Azcapotzalco subdued Culhuacan in large part with Aztec troops'; no coordinates or borough on the page.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Tepanec empire). Five pages (Tepanec, Azcapotzalco altepetl, plus Tepanec War, Itzcoatl and Texcoco pages opened for other dossiers). (1) 995 is Chimalpahin's founding year on the Azcapotzalco page; the Tepanec page puts the Tepanec arrival in the late 12th or early 13th century (footnote 1152, 1210, 1226). (2) Rulers: the page quotes Chimalpahin (Acolnahuacatl 1302-1366, Tezozomoc 1367-1426) and an alternative (Tezozomoc from about 1371). (3) No page gives the empire's area; the Valley of Mexico shape is the page's wording. Tepanec control of Chalco, Xochimilco, Coyoacan, Cuauhnahuac and Tlatelolco, and of the Toluca and Morelos valleys, is on none of the pages with a year. (4) Tenochtitlan is a vassal (start bridged to its founding, confidence 1); Texcoco is drawn as a contest from 1418 (a vassal reading is possible). (5) Tlacopan, the dissident Tepanec city that survived as the Triple Alliance's junior partner, needs its own dossier. (6) Gazetteer names needed: Colhuacan, Azcapotzalco. [Fix fx-40, 2 Nov 2026, R049] The Colhuacan conquest is dated 1377 (Colhuacan page) instead of 1385 (Azcapotzalco page; both opened); ledger/2 and the azcapotzalco_1385 keyframe use the Mexico City admin-1 for the unresolvable place 'Colhuacan' (gazetteer names needed: place Colhuacan / Culhuacan).
